focus: Exodus 24 brings the covenant at Sinai to its sealing: the people pledge to do all the LORD has said, Moses writes and reads the Book of the Covenant, and the covenant is confirmed with blood. Israel’s leaders then see the God of Israel and eat and drink before Him, and Moses goes up into the cloud of glory for forty days and forty nights.

sections.title: The LORD Summons Moses and the Leaders to Worship
sections.summary: The LORD calls Moses, Aaron, Nadab, Abihu, and seventy elders to come up and “worship from afar” (Exodus 24:1). Moses alone is to come near the LORD, and the people are not to go up with him.

sections.title: The Covenant Is Confirmed with Blood
sections.summary: Moses tells the people all the LORD’s words, writes them, builds an altar with twelve pillars, and sprinkles half the blood of the offerings on the altar. After he reads the Book of the Covenant and the people pledge obedience, he sprinkles the blood on the people and says, “This is the blood of the covenant which the LORD has made with you” (Exodus 24:8).

sections.title: Israel’s Leaders See God and Eat Before Him
sections.summary: Moses, Aaron, Nadab, Abihu, and seventy elders go up “and they saw the God of Israel” (Exodus 24:10), with a pavement like sapphire under His feet. God does not lay His hand on them, and they eat and drink in His presence.

sections.title: Moses Enters the Cloud of Glory on the Mountain
sections.summary: The LORD calls Moses up to receive the tablets of stone, and Moses goes up with Joshua, leaving Aaron and Hur with the elders. The glory of the LORD rests on Sinai like a consuming fire, and on the seventh day Moses enters the cloud and stays on the mountain forty days and forty nights.

1.brief: God tells Moses to come up with Aaron, Nadab, Abihu, and seventy elders “and worship from afar.” Israel’s leaders are invited into God’s presence, but at a distance.
1.explain:
“Now He said to Moses, ‘Come up to the LORD, you and Aaron, Nadab and Abihu, and seventy of the elders of Israel,”

God invites Israel’s leaders up the mountain. “Nadab and Abihu” were Aaron’s two oldest sons (6:23). The “seventy of the elders” represent the whole people.

“and worship from afar.”

They are to bow down at a distance. Israel’s leaders are invited into God’s presence, but at a distance.
1.notes: Nadab and Abihu later died for offering “profane fire” before the LORD (Leviticus 10:1–2). Having been near God did not protect them from judgment when they disregarded His holiness.

2.brief: Moses alone may come near the LORD, while the others stay back and the people do not go up at all. The levels of approach show both God’s welcome and His holiness.
2.explain:
“And Moses alone shall come near the LORD, but they shall not come near;”

Only Moses may come close. The leaders must stay back.

“nor shall the people go up with him.”

The people remain below. There are three levels of approach: the people at the foot, the leaders partway up, and Moses near God. The levels of approach show both God’s welcome and His holiness.

3.brief: Moses tells the people all the LORD’s words and judgments, and they answer with one voice, “All the words which the LORD has said we will do.” The people commit themselves to the covenant God has spoken.
3.explain:
“So Moses came and told the people all the words of the LORD and all the judgments.”

Before going up, Moses tells the people “all the words of the LORD,” the Ten Commandments, and “all the judgments,” the laws of 21:1–23:33.

“And all the people answered with one voice and said, ‘All the words which the LORD has said we will do.”

The people answer “with one voice.” They commit themselves to obey (compare 19:8). The people commit themselves to the covenant God has spoken.

4.brief: Moses writes all the words of the LORD, then builds an altar at the foot of the mountain with twelve pillars for the twelve tribes. The covenant is put in writing and set before God with every tribe represented.
4.explain:
“And Moses wrote all the words of the LORD.”

Moses puts the covenant in writing. This written record is the Book of the Covenant (24:7).

“And he rose early in the morning, and built an altar at the foot of the mountain,”

Early the next morning Moses builds “an altar” below the mountain.

“and twelve pillars according to the twelve tribes of Israel.”

He also sets up “twelve pillars,” one for each tribe. The covenant is put in writing and set before God with every tribe represented.
4.notes: These pillars were memorial stones, not idols. They differ from the pagan sacred pillars Israel was told to destroy (23:24). Joshua later set up twelve stones at the Jordan as a memorial (Joshua 4:1–9).

5.brief: Moses sends young men of Israel to offer burnt offerings and peace offerings of oxen to the LORD. The covenant ceremony begins with sacrifice.
5.explain:
“Then he sent young men of the children of Israel,”

Moses sends “young men” to offer the sacrifices. Aaron and his sons had not yet been ordained as priests (28–29).

“who offered burnt offerings and sacrificed peace offerings of oxen to the LORD.”

They offer “burnt offerings” and “peace offerings.” The burnt offering was wholly given to God. The peace offering was shared in a meal, celebrating fellowship. The covenant ceremony begins with sacrifice.

6.brief: Moses puts half the blood in basins and sprinkles half on the altar. The blood is divided between God’s altar and the people.
6.explain:
“And Moses took half the blood and put it in basins,”

Moses divides the blood. Half goes into “basins.”

“and half the blood he sprinkled on the altar.”

The other half he “sprinkled on the altar,” which stood for God’s side of the covenant. The blood is divided between God’s altar and the people.

7.brief: Moses reads the Book of the Covenant to the people, and they say, “All that the LORD has said we will do, and be obedient.” The people hear the covenant read and pledge their obedience again.
7.explain:
“Then he took the Book of the Covenant and read in the hearing of the people.”

Moses reads “the Book of the Covenant” aloud. The people hear exactly what they are agreeing to.

“And they said, ‘All that the LORD has said we will do, and be obedient.”

They respond a third time (19:8; 24:3), now adding “and be obedient,” literally and we will hear. The people hear the covenant read and pledge their obedience again.

8.brief: Moses sprinkles the blood on the people and says, “This is the blood of the covenant which the LORD has made with you.” The blood seals the covenant between God and Israel, words Jesus later echoes when He speaks of His own blood of the new covenant.
8.explain:
“And Moses took the blood, sprinkled it on the people, and said,”

Moses now “sprinkled” the other half of the blood “on the people.” The same sacrifice touches both the altar and the people, binding them together in covenant.

“This is the blood of the covenant which the LORD has made with you according to all these words.”

Moses names what the blood means. The covenant is ratified by blood, sealing the people’s pledge and God’s commitment. The blood seals the covenant between God and Israel. Hebrews 9:18–22 recalls this ceremony to explain that the first covenant was put into effect with blood. At the Last Supper Jesus said, “For this is My blood of the new covenant, which is shed for many for the remission of sins” (Matthew 26:28). His words echo Moses’ words here and point to the new covenant promised in Jeremiah 31:31–34.

9.brief: Moses, Aaron, Nadab, Abihu, and the seventy elders go up the mountain. The summons of verse 1 is now carried out.
9.explain:
“Then Moses went up, also Aaron, Nadab, and Abihu, and seventy of the elders of Israel,”

The summons of 24:1 is now carried out. The leaders go up the mountain with Moses.

10.brief: “And they saw the God of Israel,” with something like a pavement of sapphire under His feet, as clear as the heavens. The leaders are given a real but limited vision of God’s glory.
10.explain:
“and they saw the God of Israel.”

The narrator states it without qualification. This was a real encounter with God, though limited. Later God tells Moses, “You cannot see My face; for no man shall see Me, and live” (33:20). The leaders saw a real manifestation of God’s glory, not the fullness of His being.

“And there was under His feet as it were a paved work of sapphire stone, and it was like the very heavens in its clarity.”

The account describes only what was “under His feet.” It looked “as it were a paved work of sapphire stone,” clear and brilliant “like the very heavens.” The text gives no description of God Himself. The leaders were given a real but limited vision of God’s glory.
10.notes:
Ezekiel also saw something “like a sapphire stone” in his vision of the throne of God (Ezekiel 1:26).

The Hebrew word translated “sapphire” may refer to lapis lazuli, a deep blue stone.

11.brief: God does not lay His hand on the nobles of Israel, “So they saw God, and they ate and drank.” The covenant people’s leaders share a meal in God’s presence and live.
11.explain:
“But on the nobles of the children of Israel He did not lay His hand.”

God “did not lay His hand” on them. The text does not report what the nobles expected. Elsewhere the danger of approaching God is plain: the people at the mountain asked that God not speak with them, “lest we die” (20:19). Here God spared the leaders who saw Him.

“So they saw God, and they ate and drank.”

They “saw God,” and in His presence “they ate and drank.” The meal may have come from the peace offerings. The leaders of the covenant people shared a meal in God’s presence and lived. The covenant brought fellowship with God.

12.brief: The LORD calls Moses to come up and stay on the mountain to receive tablets of stone with the law and commandments He has written. God Himself will give the written law for Moses to teach.
12.explain:
“Then the LORD said to Moses, ‘Come up to Me on the mountain and be there;”

God calls Moses higher, to stay “on the mountain.”

“and I will give you tablets of stone, and the law and commandments which I have written, that you may teach them.”

God will give Moses “tablets of stone,” written by God Himself. Moses is to “teach them” to the people. God Himself will give the written law for Moses to teach.
12.notes: 31:18 says the tablets were “written with the finger of God.”

13.brief: Moses rises with his assistant Joshua, and Moses goes up to the mountain of God. Joshua accompanies Moses as he sets out, while Moses alone will enter the cloud in verse 18.
13.explain:
“So Moses arose with his assistant Joshua,”

Moses sets out with “his assistant Joshua.” Joshua was being prepared for future leadership.

“and Moses went up to the mountain of God.”

Moses climbs “the mountain of God.” Joshua accompanies him partway, but Moses alone will enter the cloud (24:18). Joshua is waiting near when Moses comes down (32:17).

14.brief: Moses tells the elders to wait until they return and to bring any difficulty to Aaron and Hur. Moses arranges leadership for the camp in his absence.
14.explain:
“And he said to the elders, ‘Wait here for us until we come back to you.”

Moses tells the elders to wait.

“Indeed, Aaron and Hur are with you. If any man has a difficulty, let him go to them.”

Moses leaves “Aaron and Hur” in charge. Anyone with a dispute should go to them. Moses arranges leadership for the camp in his absence.
14.notes: While Moses was away, the people pressed Aaron to make the golden calf (32:1–6).

15.brief: Moses goes up the mountain, and a cloud covers it. The cloud marks God’s presence on Sinai.
15.explain:
“Then Moses went up into the mountain, and a cloud covered the mountain.”

As Moses climbs, “a cloud covered the mountain.” The cloud marks God’s presence on Sinai.

16.brief: “The glory of the LORD rested on Mount Sinai,” and after six days God calls Moses from the midst of the cloud on the seventh day. God’s glory remains on the mountain, and Moses waits for His call.
16.explain:
“Now the glory of the LORD rested on Mount Sinai,”

“The glory of the LORD” settled on the mountain. The Hebrew verb for “rested” means to dwell or settle. It is related to the later word shekinah, used for God’s dwelling presence.

“and the cloud covered it six days. And on the seventh day He called to Moses out of the midst of the cloud.”

For “six days” the cloud covered the mountain while Moses waited. On “the seventh day” God called him. God’s glory remained on the mountain, and Moses waited for His call.

17.brief: To the children of Israel the glory of the LORD looks like a consuming fire on the mountaintop. The people below see God’s holy presence as blazing fire.
17.explain:
“The sight of the glory of the LORD was like a consuming fire on the top of the mountain in the eyes of the children of Israel.”

From below, the people saw God’s glory “like a consuming fire.” The people below saw God’s holy presence as blazing fire.
17.notes: Deuteronomy 4:24 says, “For the LORD your God is a consuming fire, a jealous God.”

18.brief: Moses goes into the midst of the cloud and up the mountain, and stays there forty days and forty nights. Moses enters God’s presence for a long time, where God will give him the pattern for the sanctuary.
18.explain:
“So Moses went into the midst of the cloud and went up into the mountain.”

Moses entered “the midst of the cloud,” into God’s presence.

“And Moses was on the mountain forty days and forty nights.”

Moses stayed nearly six weeks. During that time God gave him the pattern for the tabernacle (25–31). Moses enters God’s presence for a long time, where God will give him the pattern for the sanctuary.
18.notes: Deuteronomy 9:9 says Moses neither ate bread nor drank water during these forty days.
